Gabapentin: Initially approved as add-on therapy for refractory epilepsy; later approved for post-herpetic neuralgia (2002). Generics available since 2004. First approval/introduction: Synthesised 1974–75 (Goedecke AG / Parke-Davis); UK May 1993; US FDA December 1993.
Nortriptyline Hydrochloride: The N-desmethyl active metabolite of amitriptyline; first described and patented in 1962. First approval/introduction: Introduced 1963; US approval 1964 (Geigy).
Gabapentin 100/200/400 mg + Nortriptyline 10 mg; Gabapentin 300 mg (as listed)

Gabapentin (calcium-channel alpha-2-delta ligand) and nortriptyline (noradrenergic descending pain inhibition) act by different mechanisms; combination gives superior pain relief to either alone (Gilron et al., Lancet 2009) with lower individual doses.

Gabapentin Binds the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels in the CNS, reducing calcium influx and release of excitatory neurotransmitters (glutamate, substance P, norepinephrine). Receptor / target profile: Binds alpha-2-delta subunits of voltage-gated calcium channels, modulating calcium influx and excitatory neurotransmitter release; despite being a GABA analogue it does not act on GABA receptors.

Nortriptyline Hydrochloride Predominantly inhibits norepinephrine reuptake (and serotonin to a lesser extent); enhances descending noradrenergic pain inhibition. Fewer anticholinergic and sedative effects than amitriptyline. Receptor / target profile: Potent NET inhibitor (Ki 1.8–4.4 nM) and moderate SERT inhibitor (Ki 15–18 nM); weaker H1 and muscarinic antagonism than amitriptyline.

Summary: Well absorbed; Tmax 7–8.5 h. ~92% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2D6. Half-life 18–44 h.

Gabapentin: Dizziness, double vision, slurred speech, drowsiness, lethargy, diarrhoea. Supportive care; haemodialysis effective. Nortriptyline Hydrochloride: As for TCAs – arrhythmias, seizures, coma. ECG monitoring and supportive care.
Gilron et al., Lancet 2009 – combined gabapentin and nortriptyline gave superior pain relief to either drug alone in neuropathic pain.
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
